thread:
dana: Brainstorm: what if operator issues short-lived "lease tokens" that carry an abstract budget + immutable safety_flags. runtime redeems tokens and decides model variants. keeps operator stateless and lets runtime optimize latency/cost.
leo: Love the simplicity. How do we define the "abstract budget"? GPU millis, billing units, or something else?
nina: Keep it abstract (billing buckets). Map units -> allowed model families/quant levels on the runtime side via tenant policy. That keeps operator generic.
priya: Important constraints: tokens must be idempotent and single-namespace to avoid double-spend. runtime should send consume receipts with token_id + nonce. operator must dedupe.
kevin: Proto sketch:
```
LeaseToken {
  id: string
  units: int64
  expires_at: int64
  grace_ttl: int64  // seconds to honor inflight after draining
  safety_flags: string[] // e.g. ["no-quant", "min-recall:0.95"]
  preferred_model_family?: string
}
```
dana: Safety flags solve the "surprise-quant" incident we saw last week. If a token has no-quant, runtime must never pick a quantized variant. If it wants to, it must request a new token.
leo: Redeem flow idea: runtime calls operator.redeem(token_id, delta_units, trace_id) -> operator returns accepted_units and remaining_units. Operator keeps ledger and returns idempotent receipts.
nina: Edge cases: leader failover. operator must be tolerant: accept retries within a dedupe window and use server-side ledger to prevent double-accept. We'll document strict semantics.
priya: Also need explicit error codes: TOKEN_EXPIRED, INSUFFICIENT_UNITS, VIOLATES_SAFETY, SERVER_ERROR. makes automation deterministic.
kevin: Observability: runtime emits per-token metrics: units_consumed_by_variant, fallback_events, drain_crossings, trace_id for inflight requests. Console should show per-tenant breakdown by variant.
ops-bot: Note: autoscaler alert 2026-03-20 04:40 UTC showed 12% of pools with <30s headroom. related incident https://monitoring/alerts/6654320002 :warning:
dana: Rollout plan (ops runbook style):
1) Implement token minting + ledger in operator.
2) Implement redemption API + dedupe semantics.
3) Add safety_flag enforcement toggles (opt-in per-tenant).
4) Deploy runtime update that treats tokens as advisory until canary.
5) Flip enforcement for canary tenants, monitor dashboards.
leo: Also carve out a canary that has preferred_model_family set so we can verify output stability.
nina: I'll draft the observability dashboard (per-token timeline + variant cost).
priya: I'll draft the proto and a small migration doc (how to transition from capacity_grants to tokens).
kevin: I'll prototype the redemption API and idempotency receipts.
dana: Sync tomorrow 11am to close scope. thanks all.
